body_ar:
ما هي أفضل طريقة لتنمية الإيمان؟

لا شك أن الإيمان يزداد بالأعمال الصالحة وبالوسائل إلى الله سبحانه وتعالى فبعض الأعمال تشاهد زيادتها للإيمان، وذلك مثل نوافل الصلوات وبالأخص قيام الليل، فصلاة الليل والناس نيام، وكذلك الصدقات الخفية وكذلك تدبر القرآن وكذلك الموعظة والإنسان خال حتى تسيل دمعتاه، وكذلك زيارة القبور وعيادة المرضى ومشاهدة عجائب خلق الله، وكذلك التدبر في آيات هذا الكون الفسيح العجيب المدبر، كل هذا مما يزيد الإيمان بالله سبحانه وتعالى ويزيد محبته والتوكل عليه،

وإن من أبلغ ذلك اجتناب المعاصي، فهذه المعاصي هي التي توهن الإيمان وتضعفه، وإذا وقع الشخص في معصية انتقص من إيمانه قدر تلك المعصية، إذا كانت صغيرة انتقص من إيمانه صغير وإذا كانت كبيرة انتقص من إيمانه كبير وهكذا، فليحافظ الإنسان على إيمانه باجتناب المعاصي أولا، ثم يزيده ويحليه بزيادة الأعمال الصالحة ما استطاع إلى ذلك سبيلا، وأفضل ذلك الفرائض ثم ما تزاد به من النوافل كما صح في الحديث القدسي الشريف أن رسول الله (ص) قال فيما يرويه عن ربه عز وجل: «وما تقرب إلي عبدي بشيء أحب إلي مما افترضته عليه، ولا يزال عبدي يتقرب إلي بالنوافل حتى أحبه، فإذا أحببته كنت سمعه الذي يسمع به وبصره الذي يبصر به ويده التي يبطش بها ورجله التي يمشي بها، ولئن سألني لأعطينه ولئن استعاذ بي لأعيذنه، ولا شك أن مما ينقص الإيمان الاشتغال بزخارف هذه الدنيا والإقبال عليها، فهذه الدنيا ملهاة عن الآخرة، والآخرة التدبر فيها والتفكر فيها وتذكر هاذم اللذات الذي هو الموت مما يزيد الإيمان، أما الإغراق في الانشغال بملذات الدنيا وشهواتها والنظر إلى ما فيه أهلها فهو مما ينقص الإيمان ولهذا قال الله تعالى لرسوله (ص): {وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَى مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى (131) وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا لَا نَسْأَلُكَ رِزْقًا نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَى (132)} [طه] فعلى الإنسان أن يتقلل من النظر إلى ما لم يعطه من هذه الدنيا، وأن ينظر في الدنيا إلى من هو دونه، وأن ينظر في الدين إلى من هو فوقه فإن ذلك أجدر به أن لا يزدري نعمة الله عليه، كما أرشد إلى ذلك رسول الله (ص).
body_en:
What is the best way to develop faith?

There is no doubt that faith increases through righteous deeds and through the means that lead to God, glorified and exalted. In some deeds their increasing of faith can be observed — such as the voluntary prayers, and especially standing in prayer at night: prayer in the night while people are asleep. And likewise hidden acts of charity; and likewise pondering the Qur'an; and likewise admonition, with a person alone, until his tears flow; and likewise visiting graves, and visiting the sick, and beholding the wonders of God's creation; and likewise pondering the signs of this vast, wondrous, governed universe. All of this is among the things that increase faith in God, glorified and exalted, and increase love of Him and reliance upon Him.

And among the most effective of that is avoiding acts of disobedience, for it is these acts of disobedience that sap faith and weaken it. When a person falls into an act of disobedience, his faith is diminished by the measure of that act: if it was a small one, his faith is diminished by a small amount; and if it was a great one, his faith is diminished by a great amount, and so on. So let a person safeguard his faith first by avoiding acts of disobedience, and then let him increase it and adorn it by increasing righteous deeds, as far as he is able to find a way to it. The best of that is the obligatory acts, and then what is added to them of voluntary acts — as is soundly established in the noble divine report, in which the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said, relating from his Lord, mighty and majestic: 'My servant draws near to Me with nothing more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. And My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him; and when I love him I am his hearing with which he hears, and his sight with which he sees, and his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks. And if he asks Me, I shall surely give him; and if he seeks refuge with Me, I shall surely grant him refuge.'

And there is no doubt that among the things that diminish faith is occupying oneself with the adornments of this world and turning towards it, for this world is a distraction from the hereafter; whereas the hereafter — pondering it, and reflecting on it, and remembering the destroyer of pleasures, which is death — is among the things that increase faith. But to be immersed in preoccupation with the world's pleasures and its appetites, and in looking at what its people have, is among the things that diminish faith. That is why God, exalted, said to His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: {And do not strain your eyes towards what We have given certain groups of them to enjoy, the splendour of the life of this world, that We may try them thereby; and the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And command your family to pray, and be steadfast in it. We ask no provision of you; it is We who provide for you. And the final outcome belongs to God-consciousness} (Sūrat Ṭā Hā 20:131–132). So a person should look less at what he has not been given of this world, and should look, in worldly matters, to one who is below him, and look, in religion, to one who is above him — for that is more fitting to keep him from making light of God's favour upon him, as the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, directed.

flags.arabic: «وما تقرب إلي عبدي … ولئن استعاذ بي لأعيذنه، ولا شك أن مما ينقص الإيمان …
flags.context: the divine report quoted at the centre of the answer
options: close the quotation after لأعيذنه, as done here, and flag the source's unclosed mark
leave the quotation open as the source does
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT — QUOTATION BOUNDARY LOST. The source opens the quotation with « and never closes it, so that the Sheikh's own following sentence ('And there is no doubt that among the things that diminish faith …') runs on inside the quotation marks, as though it were part of the divine report. That is a serious defect for a text of this kind: uncorrected, it presents the Sheikh's words as God's. The boundary has been placed after lā-uʿīdhannahu, which is where the attested report ends and where the subject plainly changes. The unclosed mark is preserved in body_ar per the house rule; the English closes the quotation and the defect is flagged. A reviewer should confirm.

flags.context: how the Sheikh introduces the report
options: the noble divine report (ḥadīth qudsī), not set in Qur'anic braces
flags.note: A ḥadīth qudsī is divine speech reported by the Prophet and is not Qur'an; house style's curly braces are reserved for Qur'an and have not been used. The Sheikh says the report is soundly established (ṣaḥīḥ) and that grading is his and has been kept; he names no collection, and none has been supplied.

flags.arabic: كنت سمعه الذي يسمع به وبصره الذي يبصر به
options: I am his hearing with which he hears, and his sight with which he sees
flags.note: STYLE GUIDE §8 CONTEXT. This clause is the single most contested sentence in the report and has been read very differently across the theological schools. The English renders it as the Arabic has it, without adding the interpretive 'as' of option 3 or the temporal 'become' of option 2, either of which would take a side. The Sheikh quotes it here without comment and offers no interpretation, and none has been supplied.

hādhim al-ladhdhāt is the wording of a well-known prophetic report, quoted here as a fixed epithet rather than as a citation, and the Sheikh gives no attribution for it. Worth fixing centrally, as the phrase recurs in this corpus.
